stories.headline: US Commerce to put $2B into nine quantum firms via CHIPS Act, taking equity stakes

key_facts.fact: The US Department of Commerce signed letters of intent to provide $2.013 billion in CHIPS and Science Act incentives to nine quantum companies, and will take a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each as a condition of the funding.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Commerce today announced the signing of 9 letters of intent to provide $2.013 billion in federal incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act... The Department will receive a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each company as a condition for receiving the funds.

key_facts.fact: Two of the nine are designated 'quantum foundry' companies: IBM gets $1 billion to set up a new standalone subsidiary called Anderon in New Albany, New York to manufacture quantum-grade superconducting wafers, and GlobalFoundries gets $375 million for a domestic quantum foundry.
key_facts.excerpt: The most substantial funding is slated for the two foundry companies, with $375 million for Global Foundries and $1 billion for IBM... 'will operate as a state-of-the-art 300-millimeter quantum wafer foundry.'

key_facts.fact: The seven quantum-computing recipients are Atom Computing, Diraq, D-Wave, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum and Rigetti; Diraq receives $38 million and the other six get about $100 million each.
key_facts.excerpt: $2.013 billion in CHIPS funding will go to IBM, GlobalFoundries, Atom Computing, Diraq, D-Wave, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum and Rigetti... Diraq, which specializes in quantum computing via silicon spin qubits, received $38 million. The other six each received $100 million.

key_facts.fact: IBM said it would itself contribute an additional $1 billion to Anderon, calling it 'America's first pure-play quantum foundry'; GlobalFoundries said Commerce's stake represents roughly 1% ownership.
key_facts.excerpt: A $1 billion 'incentive' from the Department of Commerce would support the research and development efforts of a new IBM company called Anderon, 'America's first pure-play quantum foundry'... IBM said it would invest an addition $1 billion into Anderon.

key_facts.fact: Quantum stocks jumped on the news, with D-Wave and Rigetti shares gaining about 14% and 12% respectively and IBM rising nearly 4% at the open.
key_facts.excerpt: smaller firms such as D-Wave Quantum and Rigetti Computing, which are both due to receive up to $100 million in exchange for equity... The companies' shares gained 14% and 12% respectively... Its shares gained nearly 4% at the open.

stories.headline: Brett Adcock's AI hardware lab Hark raises $700M Series A at $6B valuation

key_facts.fact: Hark, an AI lab building models and hardware for an AI personal assistant, raised $700 million in a Series A round that values it at $6 billion post-money.
key_facts.excerpt: Hark, an AI lab building models and hardware for an AI personal assistant... said on Thursday that it had raised that much in a Series A round that values it at $6 billion post-money.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Parkway Venture Capital and included Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, ARK Invest, Brookfield, Greycroft, Align Ventures, Prime Movers Lab and Tamarack Global.
key_facts.excerpt: The mega-round was led by Parkway Venture Capital and included Nvidia, Align Ventures, AMD Ventures, ARK Invest, Brookfield, Greycroft, Intel Capital, Prime Movers Lab, Qualcomm Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and Tamarack Global.

key_facts.fact: Founder and CEO Brett Adcock, who also founded robotics company Figure.AI and electric-aircraft builder Archer, launched Hark in late 2025 with $100 million of his own money to build an agentic AI 'universal interface with the digital world.'
key_facts.excerpt: Founder and CEO, Brett Adcock, also the entrepreneur behind robotics company Figure.AI and electric aircraft builder Archer, launched Hark in late 2025 with $100 million of his own money.

key_facts.fact: Hark currently has 70 employees and runs a data center with Nvidia B200 GPUs; it expects to release its first multimodal models this summer, followed by hardware devices built specifically for those systems.
key_facts.excerpt: The company currently has 70 employees and runs a data center with Nvidia B200 GPUs... Hark expects to release its first multimodal models this summer... The company expects to follow that with hardware devices built specifically for those systems.

stories.headline: Bloom Energy signs up to $2.6B fuel-cell deal to power Nebius AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Bloom Energy announced a 10-year supply agreement with European AI infrastructure firm Nebius worth up to $2.6 billion in aggregate service fees.
key_facts.excerpt: The fuel cell maker announced a multi-year supply agreement with Nebius, a European AI infrastructure company, worth up to $2.6B in aggregate service fees over a decade.

key_facts.fact: Bloom will install, operate and maintain its solid-oxide fuel-cell systems across three phases, reaching 250 MW of guaranteed capacity and 328 MW of installed capacity dedicated to AI workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the agreement, Bloom will install, operate, and maintain fuel cell systems for Nebius across three distinct phases. At full deployment, the arrangement calls for 250MW of guaranteed capacity and 328MW of installed capacity.

key_facts.fact: The deal is structured so Bloom retains ownership of the systems and Nebius books the arrangement as operating expense rather than capital expenditure; Bloom's stock climbed roughly 2% on the news.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is structured so that Nebius books the arrangement as operating expense, not capital expenditure... Bloom's stock climbed roughly 2% on the news.

key_facts.fact: Nebius has been scaling rapidly, recently securing a $2 billion investment from Nvidia and a $27 billion infrastructure deal with Meta, alongside plans for a 310 MW data center in Finland by 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Nebius has been scaling rapidly, recently securing a $2 billion investment from Nvidia and a $27 billion infrastructure deal with Meta, alongside plans for a 310-megawatt data center in Finland by 2027.

stories.headline: HIVE Digital plans CAD 3.5B, 320MW AI 'gigafactory' near Toronto for 100,000+ GPUs

key_facts.fact: HIVE Digital Technologies, through its subsidiary BUZZ HPC, plans to build a 320 MW AI campus in the Greater Toronto Area designed to house more than 100,000 GPUs when fully operational.
key_facts.excerpt: Through its subsidiary BUZZ High Performance Computing, the company plans to build a 320 MW AI campus in the Greater Toronto Area, a facility designed to house more than 100,000 GPUs when fully operational.

key_facts.fact: The project carries an estimated price tag of roughly CAD 3.5 billion and targets completion in the second half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The estimated price tag: roughly CAD 3.5 billion. The targeted completion window: the second half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: BUZZ HPC has already acquired about 25 acres of land in the Greater Toronto Area for CAD 58 million as the foundation for the campus.
key_facts.excerpt: BUZZ HPC, the subsidiary leading the project, has already acquired approximately 25 acres of land in the Greater Toronto Area for CAD 58 million.

key_facts.fact: HIVE, which built its reputation mining Bitcoin and Ethereum, is pivoting its power-management expertise to AI compute infrastructure, calling the project an 'AI gigafactory.'
key_facts.excerpt: For a company that built its reputation mining Bitcoin and Ethereum, this is about as dramatic a pivot as you'll find in the digital infrastructure space... a term borrowed from Tesla's playbook.

stories.headline: EU to propose lifting sanctions on Chinese chipmaker Yangjie to avert auto supply crisis

key_facts.fact: The European Commission will propose, as early as this week, a temporary exemption from sanctions for Chinese semiconductor supplier Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology after automakers warned of supply-chain chaos.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission, the EU's executive arm, will propose the exemption for the chip manufacturer Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology as early as this week, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Yangjie was added to the EU's 20th sanctions package in April after dozens of shipments of its technology allegedly reached Russia and its products were found in drones and glide bombs used against Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese semiconductor firm was sanctioned in April after dozens of shipments of its technologies allegedly reached Russia and its products were found in drones and glide bombs used against Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: European automakers warned chip inventories would be exhausted within weeks without the derogation; any exemption would be temporary, likely lasting several months, and requires approval from all 27 EU member states.
key_facts.excerpt: European automakers warned that without the derogation, chip inventories would be exhausted within weeks, forcing production stoppages across the continent. The proposal... would still require approval from all 27 EU member states.

key_facts.fact: Yangjie had become a fallback power-semiconductor supplier after the Nexperia crisis, when the Dutch government seized Nexperia from Chinese parent Wingtech in October and Beijing retaliated with export controls, halting production at Honda, Volkswagen and Bosch.
key_facts.excerpt: Yangjie had become a crutch for sourcing components after the Dutch government seized control of Nexperia from its Chinese parent Wingtech last October. Beijing retaliated with export controls on the chipmaker's Chinese-made output, forcing temporary production shutdowns at Honda, Volkswagen, Bosch, and others.

stories.headline: Chinese dexterous-hand maker AGILINK hits $1B valuation on fourth funding round

key_facts.fact: AGILINK, a Chinese maker of high-dexterity robotic hands and grippers spun out of Zhiyuan Robotics in late 2025, closed its fourth funding round at several hundred million yuan, reaching unicorn status above a $1 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: AGILINK, a startup spun out of Zhiyuan Robotics in late 2025, closed its fourth funding round at several hundred million yuan, officially entering unicorn territory.

key_facts.fact: The raise came roughly 100 days after the company's previous financing round.
key_facts.excerpt: The raise landed approximately 100 days after AGILINK's previous financing round.

key_facts.fact: Since January, AGILINK has shipped more than 8,000 dexterous hands and over 10,000 grippers, with nearly 1,000 units active across industrial, logistics and service applications.
key_facts.excerpt: Since January, the company has shipped over 8,000 dexterous hands and more than 10,000 grippers. Nearly 1,000 units are currently active across industrial, logistics, and service applications.

key_facts.fact: Lead investors in the latest round reportedly include Baidu Ventures and Hillhouse Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: Lead investors reportedly include Baidu Ventures and Hillhouse Capital.

stories.headline: Broadcom, Meta, Applied Materials, GlobalFoundries, Synopsys launch $125M UCLA chip hub

key_facts.fact: Broadcom, Applied Materials, GlobalFoundries, Meta and Synopsys are founding partners of a new $125 million Semiconductor Hub at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering.
key_facts.excerpt: Founding partners behind the $125 million effort include Broadcom, Applied Materials, GlobalFoundries, Meta and Synopsys.

key_facts.fact: The hub focuses on energy-efficient, AI-powered chip technologies and spans chip design, software, manufacturing, equipment and advanced materials, starting with an initial five-year commitment.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial five-year commitment will establish a long-term collaboration across the semiconductor ecosystem, spanning chip design, software, manufacturing, equipment and advanced materials.

key_facts.fact: The effort is pitched as strengthening US leadership and workforce development in chip technologies critical to economic growth and national security, with faculty and student researchers working alongside the founding companies to shorten innovation timelines.
key_facts.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind Semiconductor Hub at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering aims to accelerate research, strengthen U.S. leadership and support workforce development in energy-efficient AI-powered chip technologies critical to economic growth and national security.

sources.title: UCLA Samueli School of Engineering Launches $125 Million Semiconductor Hub With Top Industry Leaders
